facts.claim: Default sandbox mode is `workspace-write` (env DSH_PERMISSION_MODE, default 'workspace-write') and approval policy `ask`.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Presets shipped: read-only/ask, workspace-write/ask, danger-full-access/never.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Approval `ask` delegates to composed answerers; `never` rejects; missing/failed answerer => `unavailable` => action fails closed; approval applies only to that request.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D01.rationale: Named presets bundle a sandbox mode with an ask/never approval policy; default workspace-write+ask; approval is one-shot per request and fails closed. No per-command allow/deny rules, and danger-full-access is one env var away.

facts.claim: sandbox-local confines commands on Linux (bwrap then Landlock), macOS (Seatbelt), Windows (ACL runner, partial) and fails with SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE instead of running unconfined.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: SAFETY.md: sandboxing, approval prompts and permission controls reduce risk but do not guarantee isolation; project has not undergone a security audit.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D02.rationale: OS sandbox (bwrap/Landlock/Seatbelt) is on by default in workspace-write mode and fails closed, but covers file effects only and the project is an unaudited dev preview.

facts.claim: SandboxMode governs file effects only; network and process policy are outside its vocabulary.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Tool catalog lists web_fetch and web_search tools (no allowlist config documented).
facts.label: from-official-docs

D03.rationale: No egress control: sandbox policy governs file effects only; web_fetch/web_search tools have no documented domain allowlist.

facts.claim: Profiles live under $DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>; layers are bundle patches, profile cordis.patch.yml, home cordis.patch.yml, --patch overlays; no repo-level config layer.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Project instruction chain (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, *.local.md) and project skills (.dsh/skills, .agents/skills) are loaded from the repo by default.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: No workspace-trust prompt found in docs/READMEs searched.
facts.label: unverified

D04.rationale: Executable configuration (plugins, MCP, policies) is only read from $DSH_HOME, not from the repo, which avoids the repo-config-before-trust class; no folder-trust prompt exists though, and AGENTS.md/skills from the repo load silently.

facts.claim: `No server is enabled by default`; each server is one dsh-mcp-client plugin row with transport stdio|streamable-http, command/args/env or url/headers; stdio env merged over scrubbed ambient env.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D05.rationale: No MCP servers by default; servers are defined only in user-owned profile files, so a cloned repo cannot add one; no allow/deny governance, tool-change detection not documented.

facts.claim: `dsh plugin --profile <name> <pnpm args>` manages plugins by forwarding to pnpm; incompatible plugins need an explicit version exemption.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Community indexes claim thousands of dsh plugins (e.g. 11,000+ listed by a third-party marketplace repo).
facts.label: third-party-report

facts.claim: SAFETY.md: project can load third-party plugins; review plugins before allowing them to run.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D06.rationale: Everything is a plugin run in-process from npm via pnpm with peer-range checks and build approval prompts, but no signing, vetting or marketplace review; large unvetted community ecosystem.

facts.claim: Credentials stored in $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; precedence stored file > env > project .env > home .env; 'this store cannot isolate secrets from the agent'.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Web UI keys are write-only; page receives a redacted descriptor.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D07.rationale: Keys in a private YAML file (write-only UI, env scrubbing for MCP) but plaintext on disk and the docs state the agent can read it; session logs may contain secrets.

facts.claim: `dsh --profile headless "job"` runs one persisted session, prints final answer, exits 0 only for completed; mounts no HTTP server or browser.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Approval `never` is the 'strict headless stance for CI and unattended runs'; with `ask` and no answerer requests fail closed.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D08.rationale: Headless profile mounts no listener, uses launch-time creds and, with default ask policy and no answerer, denies approval-gated actions; no official CI action found.

facts.claim: Memory systems are connected only through default-off reference MCP configurations.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D09.rationale: N/A (no built-in persistent memory; only optional third-party memory MCP overlays).

facts.claim: Subagent packages: spawn-in-process, fork-in-process, ACP, claude-code, codex, dsh-sdk.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Delegated children pin approval policy `never`.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D10.rationale: Sub-agent isolation not fully assessed: first-party packages delegate in-process or to external ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex); permission inheritance only partly documented.

facts.claim: Every approval request and outcome is recorded in the requesting session's audit log.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Sessions persisted by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl under $DSH_HOME/sessions.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D11.rationale: Every approval request/outcome is appended to the session audit log; sessions persist as JSONL; OTel export exists. No tamper protection or central audit.

facts.claim: DeepSeek session-log contributor sends complete unaccepted log suffixes with subsequent DeepSeek requests by default; opt-out via setting or `enabled: false`.
